terms.gloss: royal, of or belonging to a king
evidence: Cic. Rep. 1.50: quīcumque genere rēgiō nātus esset
terms.comment: The plain word for what belongs to a king: his power, his army, his family (genus rēgium). As a noun, rēgia f. is the palace (Verg. A. 8.363).

terms.gloss: kingly, regal, worthy of a king
terms.comment: Like a king, fit for a king: quiddam praestāns et rēgāle (Cic. Rep. 1.69); in Cicero chiefly of monarchy as a form of state, in the poets of royal things.

phrases.latin: cum esset habendus rēx, quīcumque genere rēgiō nātus esset
phrases.english: when anyone born of the royal line had to be accepted as king

phrases.latin: strātīque vōtīs offerunt tūs, myrrham et aurum rēgium
phrases.english: and kneeling in prayer they offer frankincense, myrrh and royal gold
